title: Great Is the Lord; His Works of Might
description: Great Is the Lord; His Works of Might in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 111, part 2, headed “The perfections of God”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great is the Lord; his works of might De-mand our no-blest songs; Let his as-sem-bled saints u-nite Their har-mo-ny of tongues.

lines: Great is the Lord; his works of might
Great is the mercy of the Lord,
And ever mindful of his word,
His Son, the great Redeemer, came
Holy and reverend is his Name,
His ways are just and pure.
They that would grow divinely wise
Our fairest proof of knowledge lies

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
